subject: Access controls implementation: PaymentsCo onboarding (SSO/SCIM, service accounts, IP allowlist)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@paymentsco.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@paymentsco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PaymentsCo onboarding — initial access controls runbook and attachments

Hi Elena / Maya,

Nice to meet you (virtually). Per our kickoff call today, attaching a concise access-controls runbook to get SSO + SCIM + network constraints staged for the pilot environment. Key asks for your side:

- Confirm SSO IdP metadata (SAML metadata URL or file).
- Confirm the primary SCIM admin account for provisioning (email + role).
- Provide source IP ranges for outbound requests and any firewall change windows.

I attached: paymentsco_sso_scim_matrix.xlsx (mapping + recommended attribute set) and ip-allowlist-template.csv (simple CSV you can paste into your firewall team).

Proposed timeline (pilot):
- Week 1: SSO test (IdP metadata + test users)
- Week 2: SCIM delta sync + service-account provisioning for API calls
- Week 3: Canary cutover for subset of traffic, verify audit logs

If helpful, we can split the work into a mutual action plan; Ben and Neha from the Red team will own the technical steps.

Thanks — I’ll leave scheduling to Ben for the detailed runbook session.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PaymentsCo onboarding — initial access controls runbook and attachments

Thanks Monica — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we schedule: 

1) IdP metadata: we currently host metadata at https://idp.paymentsco.com/metadata.xml. Is a metadata URL sufficient for your side or do you need a signed XML?
2) SCIM: we have a scoped provisioning admin (scim-admin@paymentsco.com) that can be used. Does Redwood expect SCIM to be full-sync on first run or incremental?
3) IP ranges: we can grant a temporary whitelist for testing — current CIDRs: 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/28. We’ll coordinate the firewall window with our infra team (targeting next Tuesday).

Also looping CrowdSecure (security@crowdsecure.com) who manage our perimeter firewall; they may have some suggestions on locking the management plane during sync.

Elena
VP Product Ops — PaymentsCo
elena@paymentsco.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: PaymentsCo technical handoff — SSO/SCIM/service accounts/IP

Ben / Jonas / Laura — prepping the tech plan so Ben can share a single-runbook with PaymentsCo. Notes and open items: 

- SAML/IdP: Redwood needs either the metadata URL (acceptable) or a signed metadata blob for automated import; if URL, we will fetch via HTTPS and validate TLS cert. If signed XML, we will ingest manually.
- SCIM: our onboarding code supports an initial bulk import (recommended) or incremental delta. Bulk gives a clean state for first-time provisioning; delta sync cadence is configurable (1m/5m/15m). Recommend bulk first for PaymentsCo since they have ~1.2K active users.
- Service accounts: define naming convention: paymentsco-scim-sync@redwood-sa and paymentsco-audit-ingest@redwood-sa. Need the external key rotation policy and intended token TTL. Attached draft: service-account-policy.md.
- IP allowlist & NAT: Pre-flight bench — we will ask for CIDRs and temporary elongation of rule TTL during initial sync (48-hour window) to prevent sync interruptions.
- Audit & logging: enable token-level request tracing and daily SCIM audit digest for the first 14 days.

Can Jonas provide the required SAML attribute map we expect for Roles and Entitlements? Also want to confirm rollback plan: disable SCIM provisioning and revoke service-account tokens.

I attached the service-account-policy.md with suggested rotation cadence and least-privilege roles. Once Ben has the consolidated runbook I’ll slot in the technical checklist items.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Identity & Access — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: service-account-policy.md (markdown, 3KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@paymentsco.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@paymentsco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, CrowdSecure Support <security@crowdsecure.com>
Date: 2027-09-27T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan & runbook: PaymentsCo SSO/SCIM pilot — proposed dates and owners

Hi Elena and Maya — thanks for the quick replies. Below is a concise mutual action plan (MAP) we can use as the single source of truth. I’ll post a Google Sheet to the Drive link for tracking and update the HubSpot deal.

Mutual Action Plan (pilot environment):
1) SSO smoke test (Owner: PaymentsCo / Inputs: metadata URL) — Target: 2027-10-04
   - Redwood will attempt metadata fetch and create a non-prod IdP entry.
   - PaymentsCo to provide two test users (one admin, one regular).
2) SCIM bulk import (Owner: Redwood / Inputs: scim-admin account credentials) — Target: 2027-10-11
   - Neha’s team to run an initial bulk import. Expected downtime: none; need 48-hr temporary loosened firewall rule for outbound sync.
   - Service account name used: paymentsco-scim-sync@redwood-sa (token TTL 7 days, rotation every 5 days).
3) IP allowlisting & network verification (Owner: PaymentsCo + CrowdSecure) — Target: 2027-10-11
   - PaymentsCo to add Redwood egress CIDRs for pilot: 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/28.
4) Canary cutover & audit verification (Owner: Redwood + PaymentsCo) — Target: 2027-10-18
   - Route 10% of auth traffic to Redwood-hosted endpoints; verify logs, mapping of Roles -> Entitlements.
5) Production go/no-go (Owner: PaymentsCo) — Target: 2027-10-25
   - Final rollback plan: disable SCIM sync and rotate service-account tokens; Redwood will provide a forensic export of any provisioning events in last 72 hours.

Open technical questions from Redwood:
- Elena: confirm if metadata URL is signed (you indicated URL is fine). If unsigned, we’ll validate cert and ask for a signed blob only if TLS fetch fails.
- PaymentsCo: confirm whether you want group->role mapping to be direct (group name == Redwood role) or via an attribute (we recommend direct mapping for simplicity).

Links:
- Tracker: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aPaymentsCo-Onboard
- Deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-9082

I’ve attached a single-sheet runbook in the Drive (link above). Monica — can you schedule the SSO smoke test on Oct 4 and add CrowdSecure to the firewall call?

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments referenced: runbook (Drive link), ip-allowlist-template.csv (attached inline)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@paymentsco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@paymentsco.com>, CrowdSecure Support <security@crowdsecure.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-30T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & runbook: PaymentsCo SSO/SCIM pilot — proposed dates and owners

Ben / team — this looks good and thanks for the clear MAP. Confirmations: 

- Metadata URL: https://idp.paymentsco.com/metadata.xml (served over HTTPS, cert is valid). No signed blob required for now.
- SCIM admin account: scim-admin@paymentsco.com (I’ll DM credentials to Neha’s team via our secrets channel).
- Firewall CIDRs: confirmed for pilot window (198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/28).
- Mapping: we’ll go with direct group->role mapping for the pilot.

One ask from CrowdSecure (cc’d): during the 48-hour loose window, can Redwood commit to limiting SCIM write calls to a single endpoint and provide a retry/backoff spec? Our infra team wants to avoid spikes that could trigger DDoS protections.

Quick answers: yes, we can constrain to a single SCIM endpoint and provide the exact request rate envelope ahead of time. Neha — can you confirm the expected average/sec and peak/sec for the initial bulk run?

Once Neha confirms the rate and Ben schedules the Oct 4 smoke test, we’re good to go on our side.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
VP Product Ops — PaymentsCo
